headline: Govt doubles advance tax on savings certificates profit
summary: The advance tax on profits from savings certificates has been increased from 5% to 10%, putting additional financial pressure on middle-class and pensioned investors.
details: The government has proposed increasing the advance income tax (AIT) on the profits of savings certificates from 5% to 10% in the new budget's finance bill.
This move is expected to significantly reduce the net profit for middle-class and pensioned investors, increasing pressure on their daily living costs.
M. Masrur Riaz, Chairman of Policy Exchange Bangladesh, has called for the withdrawal of this tax hike to protect small investors.
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) stated that tax return filers can claim refunds for the excess tax deducted at the source.
However, experts warn that many middle-class investors do not possess a Tax Identification Number (TIN), making it impossible for them to claim such refunds.
Finance Secretary Md. Khayeruzzaman Mojumder has stated that there have been no new changes regarding savings certificates.
caption:
Tax on savings certificate profits just doubled. Middle-class and pensioners are feeling the heat.

The government has proposed increasing the advance income tax (AIT) on the profits of savings certificates from 5% to 10% in the new budget's finance bill.

This move is expected to significantly reduce the net profit for middle-class and pensioned investors, increasing pressure on their daily living costs.

M. Masrur Riaz, Chairman of Policy Exchange Bangladesh, has called for the withdrawal of this tax hike to protect small investors.

The National Board of Revenue (NBR) stated that tax return filers can claim refunds for the excess tax deducted at the source.

However, experts warn that many middle-class investors do not possess a Tax Identification Number (TIN), making it impossible for them to claim such refunds.

Finance Secretary Md. Khayeruzzaman Mojumder has stated that there have been no new changes regarding savings certificates.

headline: 17-year wait ends: Mohammedan SC wins DPL crown after dramatic finish
summary: The traditional giants secure their first Dhaka Premier League title since 2008-09, ending a long drought in a rain-affected final round.
details: Mohammedan Sporting Club have been crowned Dhaka Premier League champions for the first time in 17 years. The victory came under dramatic circumstances at BKSP-3 on Friday.

Entering the final round, Mohammedan needed a win against Abahani and a favor from Dhaka Leopards to secure the title. They dominated their match, posting a massive 406 for four, with centuries from Parvez Emon (150) and Anamul Haque Bijoy (141).
Rain played a decisive role in the final moments. Abahani's chase was halted by rain, resulting in a 63-run victory for Mohammedan under the DLS method.
Simultaneously, at BKSP-4, Dhaka Leopards defeated Prime Bank Cricket Club by nine runs via DLS, removing Prime Bank from the title race.
This marks Mohammedan's first DPL title since 2008-09 and their first since the competition attained List A status.
Mohammedan finished the tournament with 18 points, while Abahani and Prime Bank both ended on 16 points. Abahani claimed the runners-up spot due to a superior head-to-head record.
caption:
A 17-year drought ends! Mohammedan SC has finally reclaimed the DPL crown in a dramatic, rain-soaked finish.

Mohammedan Sporting Club have been crowned Dhaka Premier League champions for the first time in 17 years. The victory came under dramatic circumstances at BKSP-3 on Friday.

Entering the final round, Mohammedan needed a win against Abahani and a favor from Dhaka Leopards to secure the title. They dominated their match, posting a massive 406 for four, with centuries from Parvez Emon (150) and Anamul Haque Bijoy (141).

Rain played a decisive role in the final moments. Abahani's chase was halted by rain, resulting in a 63-run victory for Mohammedan under the DLS method.

Simultaneously, at BKSP-4, Dhaka Leopards defeated Prime Bank Cricket Club by nine runs via DLS, removing Prime Bank from the title race.

This marks Mohammedan's first DPL title since 2008-09 and their first since the competition attained List A status.

Mohammedan finished the tournament with 18 points, while Abahani and Prime Bank both ended on 16 points. Abahani claimed the runners-up spot due to a superior head-to-head record.
